page.layout: One page of text. Ornamental border at the top, then the heading "Conclusio I." Below it, one column of numbered paragraphs. No margin notes. Catchword "Hu-" at the bottom right.

main_text.head: Conclusio I.

p.i: INfeliciter Medicum Corpus absq; ⌣Animo tractare, superius ex diuini Platonis Timæo relatum est. Animum igitur D.N.A. quâ potißimum humanũ respicit corpus, nunc hîc discutere aggredior.

main_text.p: 2. Res in primis obscura videtur, & merè spiritualis; propterea quoq; perspicua reddenda Definitionibus.

p.i: Per totum lib. prim. de Anima.

main_text.p: 3. Est igitur nihil aliud Animus, nisi principium operationum, quæ eduntur à rebus animatis, ceu nutriendi, generandi simile, &c. s. κοι. ἐνν.[?]
4. Igitur ⌣Animus fuerit Natura; quum & hæc principium motus & quietis, 2. Physicor. Philosopho fuerit definita? Haud diffiteor: Natura modò rerum Animatarum.

5. Cùm verò duplex Natura sit eidem Aristoteli, Materia, & Forma: nollem ego ⌣Materiam cum quibusdam veteribus statuere Animum, sed Formam Corporis physici, organici, potentiâ vitam habentis. 2. Ἀκροάσ.[?] Φυσ. τ. 12 & c. 2. περὶ τῆς ψυχ. τ. 6.
6. Ast de exortu Animi in corpore animato, non una omnium est sententia.

7. Sententia tamen Peripateticorum est, quod bona philosophantium pace dixerim, omnem formam ex potentia materiæ educi in actum: & propter eiusdem materiæ maleficium vicissim interire. 2. de Anima t.2.8. Metaphysic. t.6.2.v. de generat. an. c.3. ex prof. Peripateticor. p. dicter. Artem induc. Natura educere, &c. D. Scherb. D. Sut.
8. Verùm eandem exortus rationem omnibus Animæ speciebus haud attribuo.

page.notes: The ornamental border at the top is decoration and is not transcribed. The mark before "Animo", "Animus" and "Materiam" (a rounded sign like ⌣) is a printer's abbreviation sign. I did not expand it. "superius" is split at the line end ("su-" / "perius") with no visible printed hyphen; I have written it whole. The reference in paragraph 3 ("s. κοι. ἐνν.") is in small type and hard to read; the Greek is uncertain. The first Greek reference in paragraph 5 ("Ἀκροάσ.") is also uncertain. The references in paragraph 7 are set in smaller type inside the column and are copied as running text. No page number, running head or signature is printed.
